use: The everyday, slightly polite word for any shop or place to eat; plain mise sounds rougher.

example.ja: このお店、すごくおいしいよ。
example.english: This place is really good.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono omise, sugoku oishii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: このお店、すごくおいしいですよ。

notes: Often means a restaurant or bar, not just a shop.

use: Short for konbiniensu sutoa; nobody says the long form.

example.ja: ちょっとコンビニ行ってくるね。
example.english: I'm just popping to the convenience store.

examplePolite.ja: ちょっとコンビニに行ってきます。
examplePolite.english: I'll just pop to the convenience store.

use: Short for suupaa maaketto; said alone it always means the shop.

example.ja: 帰りにスーパー寄る？
example.english: Shall we stop at the supermarket on the way home?

examplePolite.romaji: Kaeri ni suupaa ni yorimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 帰りにスーパーに寄りますか？
examplePolite.english: Shall we stop at the supermarket on the way home?

notes: Not 'super' as in great; that's sugoi or saikou.

example.ja: 公園で少し歩く？
example.english: Want to walk in the park for a bit?

examplePolite.ja: 公園で少し歩きませんか？
examplePolite.english: Shall we walk in the park for a bit?

notes: Same sound as kouen (a talk or a show); context makes it clear.

use: A specific spot where something is or happens, including a spot to sit or park.

example.ja: いい場所知ってるよ。
example.english: I know a good place.

examplePolite.romaji: Ii basho o shitte imasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: いい場所を知っていますよ。

notes: Tokoro is the vaguer, softer 'place'; in questions, 'where' is doko.

english: town; part of town, the streets
use: Can mean a small town or the busy streets of a city, as in going into town.

example.ja: この町、静かで好き。
example.english: I like this town, it's quiet.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono machi wa shizuka de suki desu.
examplePolite.ja: この町は静かで好きです。
examplePolite.english: I like this town; it's quiet.

notes: Also written 街 for a busy city area; same sound.

use: Also a field or scene, like the world of music or fashion.

example.romaji: Sekai de ichiban suki na tabemono wa raamen.
example.ja: 世界で一番好きな食べ物はラーメン。
example.english: Ramen is my favourite food in the whole world.

examplePolite.romaji: Sekai de ichiban suki na tabemono wa raamen desu.
examplePolite.ja: 世界で一番好きな食べ物はラーメンです。
examplePolite.english: Ramen is my favourite food in the whole world.

notes: Sekai ichi = the best in the world, often said playfully about food or a person.

english: all over the world; the whole world
use: -juu means throughout, as in ichinichijuu (all day long).

example.romaji: Sekaijuu de ninki aru n da yo.
example.ja: 世界中で人気あるんだよ。
example.english: It's popular all over the world.

examplePolite.romaji: Sekaijuu de ninki ga aru n desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 世界中で人気があるんですよ。
examplePolite.english: It's popular all over the world.

use: The area right around your home; kinjo no = local, nearby.

example.romaji: Kinjo ni oishii pan'ya aru yo.
example.ja: 近所においしいパン屋あるよ。
example.english: There's a good bakery near me.

examplePolite.romaji: Kinjo ni oishii pan'ya ga arimasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 近所においしいパン屋がありますよ。
examplePolite.english: There's a good bakery near me.

notes: Kinjo no hito = the neighbours; tonari is the house right next door.

use: Any solid, multi-storey block of flats or a flat in one, not a mansion.

example.romaji: Eki no chikaku no manshon ni sunderu.
example.ja: 駅の近くのマンションに住んでる。
example.english: I live in an apartment near the station.

examplePolite.romaji: Eki no chikaku no manshon ni sunde imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 駅の近くのマンションに住んでいます。
examplePolite.english: I live in an apartment near the station.

notes: Apaato is a cheaper, usually low-rise wooden building.

use: A slightly formal word heard at work, in news and on forms.

example.romaji: Kyou wa jitaku de shigoto shiteru.
example.ja: 今日は自宅で仕事してる。
example.english: I'm working from home today.

examplePolite.romaji: Kyou wa jitaku de shigoto o shite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は自宅で仕事をしています。

notes: Uchi and ie are the everyday words for home.

use: A polite way to refer to another person's house or family.

example.romaji: Ashita, otaku ni ukagatte mo ii desu ka?
example.ja: 明日、お宅に伺ってもいいですか？
example.english: May I come round to your home tomorrow?

notes: Written オタク, the same sound means a geek or obsessive fan.

use: Short for koutou gakkou; covers about ages 15 to 18.

example.ja: 高校の時、野球やってた。
example.english: I played baseball in high school.

examplePolite.romaji: Koukou no toki, yakyuu o yatte imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 高校の時、野球をやっていました。
examplePolite.english: I played baseball in high school.

example.romaji: Shougakkou kara no tomodachi na n da.
example.ja: 小学校からの友達なんだ。
example.english: We've been friends since elementary school.

examplePolite.romaji: Shougakkou kara no tomodachi na n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 小学校からの友達なんです。
examplePolite.english: We've been friends since elementary school.

use: Short for chuugakkou; about ages 12 to 15.

example.ja: 中学の時、テニス部だった。
example.english: I was in the tennis club in middle school.

examplePolite.romaji: Chuugaku no toki wa tenisubu deshita.
examplePolite.ja: 中学の時はテニス部でした。
examplePolite.english: I was in the tennis club in middle school.

english: classroom; class, lessons (for a hobby or skill)

example.ja: 教室に忘れ物しちゃった。
example.english: I left something in the classroom.

examplePolite.romaji: Kyoushitsu ni wasuremono o shite shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 教室に忘れ物をしてしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I left something in the classroom.

notes: Adults hear the second sense most: ryouri kyoushitsu (cooking class), eikaiwa kyoushitsu (English school).

use: The place you grew up, or the area you live in now; jimoto no = local.

example.romaji: Oshougatsu wa jimoto ni kaeru yo.
example.ja: お正月は地元に帰るよ。
example.english: I'm going back home for New Year.

examplePolite.ja: お正月は地元に帰ります。
examplePolite.english: I'm going back home for New Year.

notes: Jimoto no tomodachi = friends from back home.

use: Usually 'X shusshin' (from X); doko shusshin? is the standard 'where are you from?'.

example.romaji: Tanaka-san tte, doko shusshin na no?
example.ja: 田中さんって、どこ出身なの？
example.english: Tanaka, where are you from?

examplePolite.romaji: Tanaka-san wa doko no shusshin desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 田中さんはどこの出身ですか？
examplePolite.english: Where are you from, Mr Tanaka?

notes: Also the school you graduated from: Toudai shusshin (a Tokyo University graduate).

use: Usually 'jikoshoukai suru' (introduce yourself); expected at first meetings, classes and new jobs.

example.ja: じゃあ、まず自己紹介しようか。
example.english: Okay, let's start by introducing ourselves.

examplePolite.ja: では、まず自己紹介をしましょう。
examplePolite.english: Well then, let's start with introductions.

use: Your number, LINE or email; renrakusaki koukan = swapping contacts, usually on LINE.

example.ja: よかったら連絡先交換しない？
example.english: Want to swap contacts?

examplePolite.romaji: Yokattara renrakusaki o koukan shimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: よかったら連絡先を交換しませんか？
examplePolite.english: Would you like to exchange contact details?
